variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: If the goal requests only one pickup and the current step shows the demonstration, locate the requested cube color before it is covered, track which container covers its location, and choose A pointing inside that container in the current execution scene. Allow small visible-centroid shifts and ignore containers covering other colors or empty locations. Output empty memory. Do not infer hidden colors from container appearance. This single-pickup path requires no further command after successful pickup; if an extra decision shows the completed pickup with the container held, choose B as the release action. For goals requesting multiple pickups, apply the following rules, starting with the memory update from the observations before selecting the subgoal. Each episode starts with A: with the hand empty and remaining_targets nonempty, pick up the container corresponding to the first point in remaining_targets. Select the current visible container at that remembered location, allowing small centroid shifts, and point inside it; the point need not equal the demonstrated center exactly. When a completed pickup leaves a container held and another target remains, choose B to put down the container. A raised hand with fingers maintaining a nonzero grasp opening after closure and lift is evidence of holding, even if object detections still report the old container center. When put-down execution shows release and the hand is empty, choose A on the first remaining target; do not select the previously picked container again merely because it is still visible. Completion of the last requested pickup satisfies the goal, so no further command is needed unless another decision is requested. For an unexpected extra decision with no targets remaining, choose B as the available release action. For ambiguous or otherwise uncovered situations, choose B if the observations indicate a held container; otherwise choose A on the visible container nearest the first remaining point. If that container is temporarily occluded, use its remembered point. Do not infer hidden cube colors from current container appearance.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: If the goal requests only one pickup, omit this field and output empty memory; use the demonstration association directly for the initial command. Otherwise, initialize this field at the first decision, when the demonstration is shown: read the requested colors in goal order and use the demonstration to match each cube to the container placed over its location. Write the ordered list of those containers' centers as [y, x] points, excluding distractors. With existing memory, inspect the execution frames for a completed pickup of the first listed container: the hand approaches its location, closes to a nonzero grasp opening, and rises with the grasp maintained. On that observed completed pickup, remove the first entry exactly once. A static container detection at the old location does not negate the observed grasp-and-lift sequence. Do not remove an entry merely because you are now selecting A, because a container is already held without a new pickup, or because the hand releases a container. Preserve all other entries and their coordinates, including across put-down execution. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
fields.annotation: For goals requesting only one pickup, omit this field and write empty memory at every decision. For goals requesting multiple pickups, this field is an ordered list of [y, x] container locations for the pickups requested by the goal that have not yet been completed. The following initialization and update rules apply only to those multiple-pickup goals. At the first decision step, associate each requested cube color with the container that covered its location in the demonstration, and list those container centers in the order requested. Ignore containers covering unrequested colors and empty distractors. Remove the first entry at the first decision step showing that its container has been successfully grasped and lifted, not at the step choosing the pickup. Putting a container down does not restore its entry. Otherwise preserve the list and its coordinates. Thus episode 7 has [[81, 95], [66, 143]] at step 1 and [[66, 143]] at both steps 2 and 3. The initial lists for episodes 4, 17, 30, and 93 are respectively [[84, 156]], [[95, 156]], [[125, 126]], and [[70, 108]]. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]

history.critique:
field remaining_targets, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Delete this field for the supplied single-pickup episodes. Each goal requests one cube color, and the only decision shows both the demonstration locating that cube and the containers covering the cubes. Incoming memory is empty, and no later decision reads the target list. The unused-field report therefore identifies a NECESSITY failure, not a demonstrated subgoal error: the target can be determined entirely from the current observation and goal. No persistent value or update event is needed; write no memory fields rather than a list such as [[92, 87]].

field remaining_targets, POLICY PROMPT
  Delete this field for the supplied single-pickup episodes. At the sole decision, the policy sees the requested color in the goal, its location in the demonstration, and the container that subsequently covers it. No carried target list is read, so persisting that locally available association violates NECESSITY. Do not initialize or update remaining_targets; use the demonstration association directly to select the pickup and output empty memory. There is no replacement field, stored value, or memory transition.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The supplied episodes request a single pickup and end after the initial command. That decision includes the full demonstration and the starting execution scene; there is no reported incorrect policy subgoal. The existing requirement to initialize and then consult remaining_targets unnecessarily routes a directly observable choice through persistent memory, violating NECESSITY. Replace it, for these single-pickup episodes, with this rule: read the requested cube color from the goal, locate that cube before it is covered in the demonstration, track which container covers that location, and choose A pointing inside that container in the current execution scene. Allow small visible-centroid shifts and ignore containers covering other colors or empty locations. Do not infer hidden colors from container appearance. Remove the remaining_targets-based completion, removal, put-down, and fallback rules from this single-pickup path; no subsequent command is needed in the supplied trajectories. This change does not establish that target memory is unnecessary for longer episodes with later decisions that no longer show the demonstration.
